title: Route billing + tail-latency multi-dimensional cube (storage-optimized)
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Console needs a single, storage-efficient analytic cube that serves two high-value use cases: (1) per-route billing attribution with customer and model-tier rollups for invoicing and cost-of-serve analysis, and (2) tail-latency diagnostics for SLO alerting and root-cause signals. Current ad-hoc tables duplicate event rows across multiple rollups and produce expensive scans for quantile calculations. This ticket proposes a canonical multi-dimensional cube (route_billing_latency_cube) built as a set of compact materialized aggregates and sketches that balance accuracy, latency, and storage cost.

Scope:
- Define the canonical schema for route_billing_latency_cube (route_id, workspace_id, model_variant, tier, day, hour, invocation_count, token_count, cost_cents_sum, p95_latency_ms_approx, p99_latency_ms_approx, tail_sketch_bytes, tail_error_margin)
- Implement ETL transformation using our warehouse (Snowflake) streams + tasks to produce compact delta-updates instead of full rewrites.
- Use compressed quantile sketches (t-digest) stored as VARIANT/BINARY + precomputed p95/p99 for fast joins.
- Add sparse-materialized partitions for hotspots (top 5% routes) with hourly granularity, while keeping daily rollups for the long tail.
- Integrate provenance columns (source_partition, ingested_at, producer_job_id) for audit and debugging.
- Expose a small set of SQL views for billing-reporting (cost attribution), SLO dashboards (tail latency trends), and an efficient API for console to fetch top tail offenders.

Why this design: Materialized aggregates + sketches dramatically reduce storage compared to keeping full invocation logs in multiple denormalized tables, while supporting near-real-time updates necessary for billing and incident triage. Hotspot-tiering avoids overprovisioning hourly granularity for low-volume routes.

Risks & Trade-offs:
- Approximate quantiles (t-digest) introduce small error; we will quantify and surface error bounds.
- Snowflake VARIANT sizing and storage costs for binary sketches need measurement; fallback is to store sketches in object storage and reference them with keys.
- Complexity of incremental tasks and backfills may require a short maintenance window for the initial rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Schema for route_billing_latency_cube defined and reviewed in Confluence with column-level descriptions and storage estimates
ETL implemented as Snowflake streams + tasks that produce incremental updates to the cube for daily and hotspot hourly partitions
Quantile sketch materialization using t-digest: documented encoding and decoding utilities in warehouse repo
Precomputed p95 and p99 fields are within agreed error bounds (p95 error < 2%, p99 error < 5%) based on sample validation runs
Cost attribution SQL view returns per-workspace per-route daily costs matching billing system within 0.5% (excluding external discounts)
SLO dashboard queries (Grafana/Looker) can render last 30 days p95/p99 trends with query latency < 5s for top-100 routes
Backfill plan and runbook documented; backfill completed for last 90 days with monitoring and reconciliation checks
